title: Drone over forest recovery landscape
alt: A sensing drone flies above a wooded mountain landscape beneath clouds.
description: The drone used to scan the mountain surface after being damaged by Hurricane Helene...Forest ecologist KC Cushman and her team from Oak Ridge National Laboratory conduct remote sensing fieldwork near Asheville, North Carolina, documenting forest recovery in the wake of Hurricane Helene. Using an Alta X drone platform equipped with a MiniRANGER-3 LITE lidar and imaging payload, alongside ground-based GPS instrumentation for precise data correction, researchers are capturing high-resolution 3D structural data on damaged and regenerating forest canopy. The work is part of Cushman's broader research into how Southeastern forests respond to disturbance — from storms to drought to wildfire — using tools that span ground, air, and satellite platforms. While centered on ecosystem recovery, the research carries direct implications for energy system resilience, helping inform how utilities and decision-makers prepare for and respond to major weather events that threaten both forests and the infrastructure running through them.

alt: A crane operator looks upward while holding an overhead crane control unit at MPEX.
description: Bret Browder, a power equipment operator at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, carefully monitors an overhead crane as he operates its controls to return it to the opposite end of the Material Plasma Exposure eXperiment (MPEX) high bay on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Following the placement of the first of six superconducting magnets, Browder prepares the crane for the next magnet transfer, supporting the continued installation and testing of MPEX's critical components. The magnets will generate the magnetic fields needed to contain and guide high-intensity plasma, advancing research into materials capable of withstanding the extreme conditions of next-generation fusion energy devices.

title: MPEX superconducting magnet installation · riggers
alt: Workers position equipment beside a large superconducting magnet at MPEX.
description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory riggers work together to align and secure the downstream helicon superconducting magnet within the Material Plasma Exposure eXperiment (MPEX) facility on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Suspended by an overhead crane, the approximately 1,300-pound magnet is carefully positioned over its permanent support structure. This first installation marks a significant step toward completing MPEX's six-magnet system, which will enable scientists to study how materials respond to intense plasma exposure and develop technologies for next-generation fusion devices.

Before installation, each magnet undergoes site acceptance testing to verify its magnetic field strength, shape and uniformity, supporting the development of materials for next-generation fusion energy systems.

title: Enriched xenon-129 cylinder
alt: A tall metal xenon-129 cylinder stands outdoors beside plants.
description: A cylinder containing enriched stable isotope xenon-129 (Xe-129) produced by the Stable Isotope Production Facility is displayed at ORNL on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026. Produced using the facility’s gas centrifuge cascade, the material represents SIPF’s largest Xe-129 batch to date. Combined with two previous batches, production has exceeded the project’s Ultimate Performance Parameter of demonstrating enrichment of more than 1 kilogram of material. Xe-129 is primarily used as a magnetic resonance imaging diagnostic tool for assessing the structure and diseases of the human lung, with approximately 1 kilogram supporting an estimated 500 MRI scans. The achievement demonstrates ORNL’s capability to produce specialized isotopes for important medical applications while strengthening the nation’s domestic isotope supply.

description: An aerial view of Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s Chestnut Ridge campus shows the Spallation Neutron Source, the Center for Nanophase Materials Sciences and the Shull Wollan Center, along with the site of the planned Second Target Station, on [day, date]. Together, these facilities and the planned expansion advance neutron scattering and materials research, strengthening U.S. scientific leadership and enabling discoveries that support energy technologies, advanced manufacturing and national competitiveness.

title: Riker computing cluster · illuminated cables
alt: Blue and green lights illuminate dense cables and computing equipment in a Riker server rack.
description: Computing equipment, network cables and illuminated status indicators fill a rack associated with Riker, a new data analysis and visualization cluster at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. The system introduces node sharing, giving users greater flexibility in how computing resources are allocated and supporting more efficient scientific analysis and visualization.

title: Riker computing cluster · server cabinets
alt: Black Riker server cabinets line a bright computing room beneath overhead cable infrastructure.
description: Server cabinets and overhead cable infrastructure line a computing room at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. The facility's new Riker cluster offers improved performance for data analysis and visualization, along with node sharing that allows users to share computing nodes. These capabilities expand access to flexible computing resources that support scientific innovation and strengthen U.S. research capabilities.

title: Riker computing cluster · technical lead
alt: A technical lead points into an open server cabinet beside the Riker computing cluster.
description: Chris Clotfelter, technical project lead for high-performance computing initiatives, points to equipment inside an open server rack associated with Riker, the new data analysis and visualization cluster at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at Oak Ridge National Laboratory on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Now available to facility users, Riker delivers improved computing performance and expanded capabilities, including node sharing, which allows users to share computing resources more efficiently. The system strengthens ORNL's advanced computing infrastructure, enabling researchers to analyze complex scientific data and accelerate discoveries that support American leadership in science and technology.
